# TermCoding — Lean 4 companion to *Term Coding: An Entropic Framework for Extremal Combinatorics and the Guessing-Number Sandwich Theorem*

[REDACTED]

This repository contains the Lean 4 development that accompanies the journal
version of the paper (Søren Riis, 2026).  Every theorem, lemma, proposition and
corollary of the paper, and the worked examples of its Sections 8 and 9, are
formalised here and checked by Lean 4.26.0 against Mathlib v4.26.0.  The
development uses no axioms beyond Lean's three standard ones (`propext`,
`Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`), contains no `sorry`, and introduces no
project axioms; this is re-checked on every push by the CI workflow.

The mathematics is the author's.  The Lean development was produced with the
help of AI assistants (drafted with ChatGPT; independently audited, corrected
and extended by Claude); all of it is machine-checked, and the checking is
what the paper's verification statement refers to.

## Principal endpoints

```lean
TermCoding.TermTheory.finiteSandwich                 -- Theorem 6.2 (finite sandwich)
TermCoding.TermTheory.maxSolutionRate_tendsto        -- Corollary 6.3 (log_n S_n(Γ) → α(Γ))
TermCoding.TermTheory.exponent_eq_labelledDependencyRateSup
                                                     -- α(Γ) = gn of the labelled dependency graph
TermCoding.LabelledDigraph.winningRate_tendsto       -- Theorem 5.6 for arbitrary finite labelled digraphs
TermCoding.Examples.C5Entropy.five_cycle_entropy_vertex
                                                     -- Proposition 7.1 (unique non-integer vertex; entropic)
```

The complete statement-by-statement map from the paper to Lean declarations,
with the exact list of what is taken as an external input, is
[`docs/PAPER_MAP_JOURNAL.md`](docs/PAPER_MAP_JOURNAL.md).

## What is not formalised

Three inputs are cited rather than formalised, exactly as stated in the paper:

1. the standard Shannon inequalities (functional dependence, submodularity,
   alphabet bound) that place the normalised entropy vector of a winning set in
   the polytope `P5` of Proposition 7.1 — this is the only unformalised step in
   the upper bound of Theorem 8.1 (`Examples/C5.lean` keeps these facts as
   explicit hypotheses; `Examples/C5EntropyPolytope.lean` proves everything
   about `P5` itself);
2. the existence of self-orthogonal Latin squares of order `n ∉ {2,3,6}` and of a
   31-self-orthogonal Latin square of order 6 (Section 8.2);
3. Kirkman's existence theorem for Steiner triple systems (Section 2 example).

The identification of the displayed instances of Sections 4.3 and 8.2 with
their normal forms is carried out by hand in the paper; Lean works with the
displayed normal-form systems.

## Build and check

Prerequisites: [elan](https://github.com/leanprover/elan) (the Lean version
manager).  The toolchain (`lean-toolchain`: `leanprover/lean4:v4.26.0`) and
Mathlib (`lake-manifest.json`: v4.26.0, commit `2df2f015…`) are pinned.

```bash
lake exe cache get          # downloads the prebuilt Mathlib (once; several GB)
lake build                  # builds every module (a few minutes after the cache)
lake env lean scripts/NamespaceAxiomAudit.lean   # fails if any TermCoding constant uses a non-standard axiom
lake env lean AxiomsAudit.lean                   # per-declaration axiom report for the headline theorems
grep -rnwE 'sorry|admit|axiom|opaque' TermCoding --include='*.lean'      # expected: no output
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs exactly these steps on GitHub Actions.

## Layout

```
TermCoding.lean                   root: imports every module
TermCoding/
  Syntax, Terms, SemanticFlattening, FiniteFlattening, VariableQuotient,
  CollisionClosure, Normalisation                     -- Section 3 (normal form)
  Diversification, LabelledGame, NeighbourGame, NeighbourCardinality,
  LabelledDependencyGraph, LabelledDigraphGame,
  OrdinaryGame, FunctionalCompletion                  -- Sections 4–5 (games)
  Product, Cardinality, Alphabet, Asymptotics         -- Proposition 5.5, Theorem 5.6
  BlockEmbedding, Sandwich, FullSandwich,
  OrdinarySandwich, Exponent, SystemExponent          -- Section 6 (sandwich, exponent)
  Examples/C5, C5EntropyPolytope, C5EntropyRealisation-- Proposition 7.1, Theorem 8.1
  Examples/PartialSOLS, SDOS, SDOSExponents           -- Lemmas 8.3–8.5, Proposition 8.6
  Examples/NetworkRedundancy                          -- Section 8.3
  Examples/Dispersion, DispersionTermCoding           -- Proposition 9.2
  Examples/ArgumentPositions                          -- Remark 4.7
AxiomsAudit.lean                  #print axioms for the headline declarations
scripts/NamespaceAxiomAudit.lean  namespace-wide axiom allowlist check (used by CI)
scripts/relay_verify.py           exhaustive check of the relay values (not used by the paper)
docs/                             paper ↔ Lean map; archived pre-audit ledgers
```

## Paper correspondence

Lean models the paper's labelled game first as one local rule per equation
occurrence, reading the ordered argument tuple; `NeighbourGame.lean` and
`NeighbourCardinality.lean` prove that collapsing repeated positions to the
paper's distinct in-neighbour set does not change the optimum (Remark 4.7).
`LabelledDependencyGraph.lean` constructs the paper's two-layer labelled
dependency graph (Definition 5.9) and proves exact equality of finite optima
(Proposition 5.10).  `LabelledDigraphGame.lean` encodes every finite labelled
digraph as a term system with one occurrence per constraint vertex, so that
Proposition 5.5 and Theorem 5.6 hold for arbitrary finite labelled digraphs and
ordinary digraphs with sources, and identifies the paper's exponent `α(Γ)` with
the guessing number of the labelled dependency graph (Corollary 6.3).
`Examples/C5EntropyPolytope.lean` and `Examples/C5EntropyRealisation.lean`
prove Proposition 7.1: over the polytope of polymatroids with the five-cycle
dependence equalities and unit alphabet bounds, `h([5]) ≤ 5/2` with a unique
maximiser `h*(S) = |S ∪ (S+1)|/2`, a non-integer vertex, which is the
normalised Shannon entropy vector (defined explicitly) of the uniform
distribution on the `m^5` winning configurations of the square-alphabet
strategy of `Examples/C5.lean`.
